title: slugify returns the title unchanged instead of a URL-safe slug
goal: slugify(title) turns a title into a lower-case, dash-separated slug made only of a-z, 0-9 and dashes, so it can be put in a URL.

criteria.text: Giving slugify a title returns a slug that can be put in a URL, so "Hello World" becomes "hello-world".
The slug is lower case, so "Hello" becomes "hello".
A space between words becomes a dash, so "big world" becomes "big-world".
Several spaces in a row become one dash, so "hello   big world" becomes "hello-big-world".
Characters other than a-z, 0-9 and spaces are dropped, so "héllo, wörld 42!" becomes "hllo-wrld-42".
Digits are kept in the slug, so "top 42" becomes "top-42".

title: slugify returns the title unchanged instead of a URL-safe slug
goal: slugify(title) turns a title into a lower-case, dash-separated string that can be put in a URL.

criteria.text: slugify returns a slug that can be put in a URL instead of the title it was given, so "Hello World" becomes "hello-world".
Upper-case letters come back lower-case, so "Hello" becomes "hello".
A run of spaces between words becomes exactly one dash, so "hello   big world" becomes "hello-big-world".
Letters outside a-z and punctuation are removed from the slug, so "héllo, wörld 42!" becomes "hllo-wrld-42".

title: slugify returns the title unchanged instead of a URL-safe slug
goal: slugify(title) turns a title into a lower-case, dash-separated string of a-z and 0-9 that can be put in a URL.

criteria.text: Passing a title to slugify returns a slug that can go in a URL, so "Hello World" becomes "hello-world".
Upper-case letters are turned into lower case, so "Hello" becomes "hello".
A space between words becomes a dash, so "big world" becomes "big-world".
Several spaces in a row become one dash, so "hello   big world" becomes "hello-big-world".
Punctuation is dropped, so "42!" becomes "42".
Accented letters are dropped rather than converted to a plain letter, so "héllo" becomes "hllo".
Digits are kept, so "42" stays "42".

title: parseDuration is an unimplemented stub: it returns null for every input instead of seconds
goal: parseDuration(text) turns a duration string such as "1h30m" into a total number of seconds, and returns null for text that is not a duration.

criteria.text: A duration written as hours and minutes comes back as the total number of seconds, so parseDuration("1h30m") returns 5400.
A number followed by "s" is counted as seconds, so parseDuration("45s") returns 45.
A number followed by "m" is counted as minutes of 60 seconds each, so parseDuration("2m") returns 120.
A number followed by "h" is counted as hours of 3600 seconds each, so parseDuration("1h") returns 3600.
Hours, minutes and seconds together are added up, so parseDuration("1h30m15s") returns 5415.
A smaller unit placed before a larger one is rejected, so parseDuration("30m1h") returns null.
The same unit used twice is rejected, so parseDuration("1h1h") returns null.
A number with a unit that is not h, m or s is rejected, so parseDuration("1x") returns null.
An empty string is not a duration, so parseDuration("") returns null.
Text with no number in it is not a duration, so parseDuration("abc") returns null.
A number with no unit is taken as seconds, so parseDuration("90") returns 90.
A part may be a decimal number, so parseDuration("1.5h") returns 5400.
A space between parts is allowed, so parseDuration("1h 30m") returns 5400.
Unit letters may be upper case, so parseDuration("1H30M") returns 5400.
